title: The Post-Mauryan Kingdoms: Indo-Greeks, Kushanas, and Satavahanas

questions.question: The dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander (Milinda) and a Buddhist monk is recorded in which Pali text?
questions.rationale: The Milindapanho ('Questions of King Milinda') records Menander's debate with the monk Nagasena, by whose teaching the king is said to have accepted Buddhism.

questions.question: The Sudarshana lake, rebuilt and praised in the Junagadh rock inscription, was first excavated under which ruler?
questions.rationale: Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription (c. 150 CE) says the lake was first excavated for Chandragupta Maurya by his governor Pushyagupta and improved under Ashoka, before Rudradaman rebuilt it.

questions.question: India's first substantial gold coinage was issued by which ruler?
questions.rationale: Vima Kadphises of the Kushana dynasty issued the first substantial gold coins (dinars), stamped with Shiva and the bull and modelled on Roman weight standards.

questions.question: The era of 78 CE, which India still uses as the Shaka era, is associated with which king?
questions.rationale: Kanishka I is remembered for the era beginning 78 CE, later known as the Shaka era, though the exact date of his accession remains debated.

questions.question: Under Kanishka, the Fourth Buddhist Council was held in:
questions.rationale: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir under Kanishka's patronage, where the Sarvastivada canon was committed to writing; the First and Second were at Rajagriha and Vaishali.

questions.question: Gautamiputra Satakarni's title Trisamudratoyapitavahana proclaims that his horses drank from:
options: The waters of the three seas
The Indus and its five tributaries
questions.rationale: The title means 'whose horses drink at the waters of the three seas', recorded in his mother Gautami Balashri's Nashik inscription after his victory over the Shakas.

questions.question: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, which lists Indian ports and trade goods, was written by:
questions.rationale: The Periplus is a first-century CE Greek trading handbook by an unknown author describing Red Sea and Indian Ocean routes, ports like Muziris and Barygaza, and their exports.

questions.question: Arikamedu, excavated by Mortimer Wheeler in 1945, is best known as evidence of:
questions.rationale: Arikamedu (Poduke) near Pondicherry yielded Arretine ware, wine amphorae, and Roman lamps alongside Tamil bead-making, showing direct Roman trade with the Tamil coast.

questions.question: The Gathasaptasati, about 700 love lyrics in Prakrit, is attributed to the Satavahana king:
questions.rationale: Hala, a Satavahana ruler, is traditionally credited with the Gathasaptasati (Sattasai); his court also had the storyteller Gunadhya, author of the Brihatkatha.

questions.question: Which Buddhist art school used blue-grey schist and showed Greco-Roman influence in drapery and hairstyle?
questions.rationale: The Gandhara school of the Peshawar valley carved the Buddha in blue-grey schist with Hellenistic drapery and wavy hair; Mathura used red sandstone in a more indigenous style.
